newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on harvest slowdown.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on harvest slowdown.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a slowdown in harvesting of hard red winter wheat and on oversold signals, traders said.
Cash grain dealers said rain halted the harvest early Tuesday in portions of southern Kansas, northern Texas and parts of Oklahoma.
As of Sunday, fourteen percent of the winter wheat crop had been harvested, above five percent the previous week but behind 27 percent harvested a year earlier and 22 percent average, USDA said.
USDA Monday said as of Sunday 67 percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was good to excellent, above the 61 percent in that category a week ago.
But many traders said the market gained slightly on signals it was oversold and due for a bounce.
The July closed Monday with a nine-day relative strength index of 19 percent and recovered to 24 percent during Tuesday's session. An RSI of 30 or less is viewed as an oversold market.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed 1-1/2 to 3-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with July up 2-3/4 at $3.32-1/2 a bushel. September was up two cents at $3.39.
LFG Futures bought two million bushels of September, Refco Inc bought two million bushels each of July and September, traders said.

In spread trading, ABN Amro-Chicago Corp did four million bushels of July/December at 19 to 20 cents, E.D. and F. Man International spread two million July/September at 7-1/2 to 7-3/4 cents and did two million July/December at 19 to 20 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 24,236 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 400 September $3.60 calls at 10-1/2 to 10-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, below the 4,766 traded Monday.
